correctness.rationale: Nine degree-four point vertices and twelve degree-five line vertices give the affine-plane incidence graph with four added triangles (48 edges, cycle rank 28). Degrees distinguish the types, and preserving incidences then forces an affine collineation; all affine collineations preserve parallel-class triangles. Independent reduced-Laplacian Smith calculations give (3,3,21^8). In the degree-zero basis, quotienting by all action differences correctly computes coinvariants; automorphism-invariance and perfection of the monodromy pairing identify their dual with fixed classes, including for the full Hessian subgroup. Independent conjugacy enumeration, rank computations for every action and integer Smith forms with two sinks agree with all eleven rows (eight different groups). The same computation confirms trivial common subgroup invariants; for the two trace-distinct classes of order eight the vertex and edge cycle data agree, as do the fixed groups. Weil pairing gives the stated determinant restriction (inverting q has the same residue mod 3). No claim of realizing every class or identifying this abstract fixed group with a Néron group is required.
residual_risks: Arithmetic realization over particular finite fields and comparison to reduction of a particular model are outside the claim.

value.rationale: The classical arrangement provides a motivated global finite action, whose critical group and graph cycle counts alone do not decide integral fixed torsion. The exhaustive class table gives a reusable exact invariant, including the modular characteristic-three effects and the difference between individual and simultaneous fixed classes. This does not require conflating graph and Néron groups.
residual_risks: Not an arithmetic realization theorem or a classification of the full integral representation.
